analysis:
The supplied units are documentation-only head text of CHANGELOG.md (lines 160-554) for the v0.10.6 candidate. No source code, configuration, or workflow changed in the supplied evidence, so no executable security regression can be established from these units.

I examined the changelog claims against the retained threat-model entries. Entries that touch security-relevant behavior:
- Per-tenant cluster prefix caches (lines 294-296): both ranks key prefixes and SSD records by a SHA-256 digest of the cache scope, never the scope itself. This is consistent with T-041 scope separation and the HMAC-keyed names; the claim is documented only.
- Quantized SSD prefix records (lines 471-476): the codec is lossy and the ranks bind precision into the load agreement. This is a behavior change relevant to T-041 at-rest posture, but no at-rest metadata change is described.
- Cluster runtime facts and the pair-serving grant (lines 415-421): public qualification of GLM-5.3-Flash and Qwen3.8-27B is declared as an owner decision. Lines 419 admit that no pipeline ran on two M5 Ultras and that GLM has no TP cross-cable record. This matters for T-054, T-056 and TB-011, and the next pass should check that the platform-owned policy matches the claim.
- Coordinator and cluster member behavior (lines 186-190, 203-206, 454): a local-only fallback applies when the coordinator lacks cluster support, and the member-role check is unchanged. The grant lease and resume path touch T-053, so the real code needs a check of resume binding and revocation.
- New cluster surfaces (lines 436-437, 457-458): a LaunchAgent, reap and cancel-all commands that signal processes only when the pid and start time match, and a local relay. These introduce new local attack surface, since a same-UID process could abuse them.
- Local-only serving keys (line 188): a token shared with `start --local`.

The actual implementation is not in this batch, so these remain unverified contracts and not findings. The threat model does not yet cover a TB for the cluster link, the cluster control channel, or a cluster relay and process-reaper surface. Integration should consider whether a threat-model update is needed. The patch excerpt is truncated, so full-file coverage is limited to the supplied lines.
